# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
...

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid
src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims:

set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &

content.text:
I made the dashboard change. Two of the four tests in the spec (2 of 4) pass. The other two still fail, each at a step that has nothing to do with the dashboard. Both of those steps come before the test reaches the dashboard checks, so the new counts haven't been checked in those two tests.

**The change:** the steward's dashboard (`dash-pending-count`, `dash-review-count`, `dash-overdue-count`) now counts over the sheet and all its descendants. Each sheet in the tree is counted the way that sheet itself shows it: its own claims, rates, settings and today. Who sees the counts hasn't changed: only someone who is a steward on the sheet being viewed. I reused the tree walk the consolidated figures panel already does, sharing its cached query, so the panel and dashboard don't fetch the descendants twice. The edits are in `features/header/dashboard.slot.tsx` and `features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`; the panel now also tracks an overdue count per sheet.

**A bug fix the spec also needed:** on a part-settle, the `CLAIM_SPLIT` audit line wrote `into=` *after* the new claim was settled, so it carried the settle's number (`into=FY2026-1`). The spec expects the number the claim had when it was split, which is blank. It now records that, which brings the line in line with its own doc comment. Files: `PartSettle.java`, `ApplyPartSettle.java`, `AuditPartSettle.java`. Scenario 3 now passes.

**Still failing:**

1. **"dashboard over tree", line 48.** On the child sheet, clerk `wes` settles Cy's open claim (amount 10.00, due 1.00, opened by `uma`), and the test expects this to be refused. Under the current rules it's allowed: the due is under the 1.50 clerk limit and `wes` didn't open or edit the claim. The audit log shows it settling as `FY2026-1`. I couldn't find a rule that should refuse it. It also wouldn't change any dashboard count the test checks.
2. **"scenario 1", line 451.** After a merge, the test expects the two moved claims, which have 1 proof each, to show 0 receipts and 0 photos. The app is built to count a proof added without a kind as a receipt (receipts = proofs − photos), and one of these claims even had a receipt added explicitly. Passing would mean changing how proof kinds are counted or what a merge does to them, which is outside this request.

I didn't change either of those behaviours, because each would mean rewriting a documented rule for no reason the request gives. If you want the app to match those two expectations anyway, tell me which rule should change and I'll do it.
